footnotes: From pre-tax income to net income to Chimera Investment: after $86.0M of preferred dividends. The income statement doesn't separate operating from non-operating items in a form this page can follow, so costs and expenses are shown in total down to pre-tax income. The 10-K reports no separate capital expenditures, so free cash flow equals operating cash flow.

Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC (income statement lines as the filing presents them); free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: The company had no revenue in 2025. Operating income rose 32.2% to $233M, a 0.0% margin.
Net income rose 59.9% to $144M, or $1.72 per share. Operating cash flow was −$249M and free cash flow −$249M, versus $206M; Chimera Investment returned $123M through dividends.
